title: Dantzig Simplex Termination (Open)
body_html:
Dantzig Simplex Termination (Open)

This is an open issue for the Dantzig ordered-field proof route. The Loomis route (Minimax via the All-Ones Specialization of Loomis) already closes the $\mathbb{R}$-version of the minimax theorem; this node captures the one remaining gap that prevents the Dantzig route from doing the same over an arbitrary linearly ordered field.

What is open

The only sorry in MinimaxDantzig.lean is the top-level dantzig_minimax theorem. Its proof needs to combine the already-proved algebraic scaffolding (pivot correctness, lex monotonicity, strategy extraction) into a terminating simplex iteration.

Concretely, the missing step is to show: starting from initialState_exists, repeated application of dantzigPivot driven by the optimality test ([Dantzig (15)]) reaches an isOptimal basis in finitely many pivots.

Why the existing scaffolding is not enough

The Lean development already supplies:

  • a basis-state data structure with a lexicographic invariant on the rows of $B^{-1}$;
  • dantzigPivot_lexCond — pivots preserve lex positivity of rows $\ge 1$;
  • dantzigPivot_beta0_decrease — pivots strictly decrease the leading row $\beta_0$ in lex order, which rules out cycles;
  • optimal_basis_minimax — at an optimal basis, the extracted strategies satisfy the minimax inequalities;
  • extractPlayerII_* — Player II extraction from the BFS data.

What is not established is that there are only finitely many distinct basis indices over the augmented column set $\{P_0, P_1, \ldots, P_n, U_1, \ldots, U_m\}$, and that the strict lex descent on $\beta_0$ plus the finite basis-index set forces finite termination.
proof_html:
plan

  1. Basis index tracking. Add a structure refinement to DantzigState recording which augmented columns form the current basis. Show that dantzigPivot swaps exactly one column index.
  2. Finite basis set. The set of possible bases is a subset of $m$-element subsets of $\{P_1, \ldots, P_n, U_1, \ldots, U_m\}$, hence finite.
  3. Finite descent. Combine the strict lex decrease of $\beta_0$ from dantzigPivot_beta0_decrease with the fact that each basis determines $\beta_0$ uniquely (since $\beta_0$ is row $0$ of $B^{-1}$). This rules out revisiting a basis, so the algorithm terminates in at most as many steps as there are $m$-element subsets of the $n+m$ augmented columns.
  4. Wrap-up. At the terminal basis, the optimality test must hold (else another pivot would apply, contradicting termination). Apply optimal_basis_minimax and extractPlayerII_guarantee to close dantzig_minimax.

References

  • [Dantzig, Section 3] Dantzig, A Constructive Proof of the Min-Max Theorem, docs/dev/references/Dantzig, CONSTRUCTIVE PROOF OF THE MIN-MAX THEOREM.pdf. Termination of the simplex algorithm via lex-monotone pivots and basis tracking.
